sonnet.problem: The card says God renamed Jacob 'Israel' and cites only Genesis 32:28. That verse has an unnamed 'he' speaking, so the cited verse doesn't state that God did it. The claim goes beyond the text it cites.
sonnet.rule: When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

sonnet.problem: The true/false statement joins two claims ('run and not grow weary' and 'walk and not faint') in one statement, so it isn't a single claim.
sonnet.rule: A true or false statement tests one claim.

sonnet.problem: The joke is the same idea and punchline shape as Stop 1 card 16: 'Friend,' followed by a self-deprecating line about hopping and limited physical ability. It repeats within the lesson.
sonnet.rule: Each joke idea, comparison and punchline shape is used once per lesson.

sonnet.problem: The question says 'the one lacking such an offering'. 'Such an offering' points back to the gold-overlaid idol on the previous story card, which the baker can't see, so the question lacks context.
sonnet.rule: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

sonnet.problem: The setup card says God 'brings the princes to nothing and makes the rulers of the earth meaningless.' That already rules out the wrong answers 'flourish' and 'multiply'.
sonnet.rule: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
